clue.text: Capital - not for investment in pudding

indicators.note: an investment is something put into a venture, so one word is placed inside the other

blocks.note: sago is a starchy milk pudding
anti means against, the opposite of being for something

explanation.surface: A financial warning: the money is not for sinking into a pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Investment' here means being put inside, not money; the opposing word sits within the pudding after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chilean seat of government is a city named after Saint James, so it fits a national capital.

clue.text: Scots know about no African

indicators.note: about suggests turning round, so the word for no is read backwards

blocks.note: ken is the Scots verb meaning to know
nay is an old word for no

explanation.surface: Scottish people knowing a thing or two about refusal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'concerning' in the surface but turns the second word round.
explanation.definitionFit: Kenyan is the demonym for someone from Kenya, a country in East Africa.

clue.text: Dog legs taken by actress and singer

blocks.note: pins is slang for legs
Cher is the American singer who also won an Oscar for acting

explanation.surface: A dog's legs being claimed by a celebrity who both sings and acts.
explanation.definitionFit: The pinscher is a breed of German guard dog, as in the Doberman pinscher.

clue.text: Did Sue and Dot dash off?

indicators.note: to dash off is to rush away in a scramble, suggesting the letters scatter

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about whether two women hurried away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Did' here is the habitual past, as in 'I did go there every week'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'used to' expresses a past habit, which the auxiliary 'did' can also convey.

clue.text: See birds with bread

definitions.note: the answer is plural, naming the bread in its baked units

blocks.note: lo is an old exclamation meaning look or see
Aves is the Latin name of the class of birds

explanation.surface: An invitation to watch birds being fed with bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Loaves are shaped and baked portions of bread.

clue.text: One hears principal songs

indicators.note: what one hears is the sound of a word, so the spoken form counts here

blocks.note: a principal is the head person, a leader

explanation.surface: Someone listening to the main songs in a concert.
explanation.definitionFit: Lieder are German art songs, typically for solo voice and piano, by composers such as Schubert.

clue.text: Almost cents is all you need for Chinese food

indicators.note: almost means not quite the whole, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: a dime is an American coin worth ten cents
the sum is the total amount required

explanation.surface: A cheap meal: a few cents buys all the Chinese food you need.
explanation.walkthrough: A dime is the US ten-cent coin, so 'cents' stands for it here.
explanation.definitionFit: Dim sum is a Cantonese style of small dumplings and snacks served in steamers.

clue.text: Soldiers capturing more than half of India in 1759 battle

indicators.note: more than half keeps the majority of a word's letters and discards the rest
to capture is to take and hold inside, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: men is the usual crossword term for soldiers
taken as written

explanation.surface: An account of troops seizing most of India in a historic campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: India has five letters, so three of them count as more than half.
explanation.definitionFit: Minden in Germany was the site of a Seven Years' War victory by British and allied forces in 1759.

clue.text: Working and keeping time is not compulsory

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within, so one word sits inside another

blocks.note: an era is a period of time
something not compulsory is left to choice

explanation.surface: A statement about workplace rules: clocking in is voluntary.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that is operational is functioning and in use.

clue.text: Upper class officer shot

blocks.note: Gen is the abbreviation for general
a shot is an attempt

explanation.surface: A posh military officer being shot.
explanation.definitionFit: The gentry are the landed families ranking just below the nobility in British society.

clue.text: Father with pathetic girl in California city

blocks.note: pa is an informal name for father
sad can mean pitiful or pathetic
Ena is a girl's name, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A dad with his miserable daughter somewhere in California.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasadena is a city near Los Angeles, home of the Rose Bowl.

clue.text: Star going round in luggage van

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the words that follow
going round means turning about, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word into the start of the second

explanation.surface: A celebrity riding about in the baggage car of a train.
explanation.walkthrough: In luggAGE Van, read backwards, sits VEGA.
explanation.definitionFit: Vega is the brightest star in the constellation Lyra.

clue.text: No other ark made land

indicators.note: made means constructed, so the letters are put together into a new form

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Noah's vessel was unique, the only one to reach dry ground.
explanation.definitionFit: North Korea is a country, and land can mean a nation or territory.

clue.text: Lack of shelter I depend on? Only in part

blocks.note: having no tent means having no shelter
taken as written
to rely on is to depend on

explanation.surface: A camper wonders whether they must rely on having no cover.
explanation.walkthrough: NO TENT plus I plus RELY makes NOT ENTIRELY, with the word break moved.
explanation.definitionFit: Something true only partly is true but not wholly or completely.

clue.text: Art works: topless things and other things on top

indicators.note: topless means with the top removed, so in a down entry the first letter goes
on top in a down clue puts this piece above the other, so it comes first

blocks.note: etc, et cetera, means and other things
taken as written

explanation.surface: A list of art pieces, some apparently nude, with more items stacked above.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless' suggests nudity in the surface but simply drops a first letter; in a down entry, 'on top' means earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: Etchings are prints made from metal plates incised with acid, a classic fine-art medium.

clue.text: Game played by kids in meadow for recreation, without parental guidance

indicators.note: recreation read as re-creation means making again, so the letters are rebuilt
without in its old sense means outside, so one piece wraps around another

blocks.note: a lea is a poetic word for a meadow
PG is the film rating for parental guidance
taken as written

explanation.surface: Children playing in a field, unsupervised by adults.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' is used in its old sense of outside, so the film-rating letters wrap the reworked word.
explanation.definitionFit: Leapfrog is a playground game in which children vault over each other's bent backs.

clue.text: Prologues from Icelandic, Norse tales, Russian or Swedish prologues

indicators.note: a prologue comes at the start, so each following word supplies its opening letter

blocks.clueFragment: Icelandic, Norse tales, Russian or Swedish
blocks.note: the initial letters of these six words

explanation.surface: A survey of the opening sections of Nordic and Russian literature.
explanation.definitionFit: Intros are introductions, the opening parts that come before the main work.

clue.text: The colour of treacle that's not quite off

indicators.note: not quite means just short of complete, so the final letter drops
off means gone bad, so the letters are spoiled into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Describing the hue of syrup that is nearly past its best.
explanation.walkthrough: TREACLE without its last letter is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret names a deep purplish red, taken from the red Bordeaux wine.

clue.text: Crisp notes corrupted policemen

indicators.note: corrupted means spoiled or altered, so the letters are put out of order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Bent coppers taking fresh banknotes as bribes.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspectors are police officers of a rank above sergeant.

clue.text: Forgo one's turn - I am frequently appearing

blocks.note: to pass in a game is to skip your go
contracted as I'm

explanation.surface: A player declining a turn because they keep showing up.
explanation.definitionFit: Passim, Latin for here and there, marks a word or name found throughout a text.

clue.text: Tame naval vessel expected

blocks.note: short for submarine
due means expected to arrive

explanation.surface: A placid warship is scheduled to arrive.
explanation.definitionFit: To subdue is to bring under control, the verb sense of making something docile.

clue.text: Clever learner in Lincoln

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the name that follows

blocks.note: Abe is the nickname of Abraham Lincoln
L is the learner-driver plate letter

explanation.surface: A bright student enrolled in the city of Lincoln.
explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln looks like the English city but is the US president.
explanation.definitionFit: Able means skilful and competent, a close synonym of clever.

clue.text: Instruments employed by one beginning to cultivate a vegetable

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, which alone is kept

blocks.note: the brass are a family of wind instruments
Roman numeral one
opening letter of the word
taken as written

explanation.surface: Tools used by a gardener starting to grow vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: Brassica is the plant genus of cabbages, sprouts and broccoli, so stands for that vegetable.

clue.text: Support the rear at the front

indicators.note: the rear is the back end, so only the closing letter of the word is kept

blocks.note: to be for something is to support it
closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: An instruction to prop up the back while standing ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: Support has to be read as two words, BE FOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Before can mean ahead or in front, as in standing before the judge.

clue.text: Fortune's arms for little birds with no go

indicators.note: with no means lacking, so the named letters are removed

blocks.note: goslings are young geese
taken as written, the letters removed

explanation.surface: Fledgling birds stuck in the nest, unable to fly.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet speaks of 'the slings and arrows of outrageous fortune', so slings are fortune's weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: Slings are the weapons, or arms, that fortune hurls in Hamlet's soliloquy.

clue.text: Ejected ticket seller turned up first

indicators.note: turned means flipped over, so the short word is read backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
a tout resells tickets at inflated prices

explanation.surface: A ticket tout thrown out of a venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' places the reversed piece before TOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To put out is to expel or throw someone out, here in the past participle.
